title: I deposted $25,000 into Public, connected it via MCP to Claude, and let it trade. I'm up over $3,000
author: NextgenAITrading
selftext:
I created the Public Portfolio Challenge, an open challenge where I watch AI agents build algorithmic trading strategies to manage over $25,000.  

So far, I'm destroying the market. 

The book trades options on high-momentum stocks in my personal watchlist. I trained it using walk forward optimization, and deployed it to Public via OAuth.with my platform. 

You can see the exact rules, the trading strategies, and my updates for free. I even have an open-source GitHub repo where you can download skills to follow along in Claude Code or Codex.

Happy to answer any questions below!

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: Publishing the rules and the live portfolio is the right level of transparency. A 12.7% gain on options of high-momentum stocks in a rising market can come mostly from leverage and exposure, so I'd show the result next to the same watchlist held in shares and SPY over the same dates, plus max drawdown and the number of trades. Since the watchlist is personal, I'd also ask how it was chosen: a list picked after those stocks moved is itself a form of look-ahead, even with walk-forward optimization on the rest. Earnings and macro dates drive options P&L, and Cymetica's EventTrader (event timing for earnings and macro releases) is one source for splitting results around them.

replies.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
replies.body: Fair enough, and good that the SPY comparison is on the page. One suggestion is to keep a dated, frozen copy of the watchlist so later results can be judged against what you actually knew at the time. The 10.76% versus 7.93% gap is also small for an options book, so I'd look at the drawdown and the worst day next to it. Thanks for the open answer.
